headline: Russia will only pretend to negotiate until spring 2027

sources: Lithuanian President Gitanas Nauseda, interviews to WELT and Onet, Nov 6
fault_line: Is Putin really about to test Article 5 -- or is this fear-mongering to keep NATO spending and Ukraine aid flowing?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Nauseda on the record] 'The Russians want to test whether we will respond or not. Putin is getting closer and closer to testing Article 5, which obliges NATO to assist an ally that has come under attack.' Lithuania has received intelligence indicating the possibility of further Russian provocations. He does NOT consider a conventional Russian attack on NATO territory likely for now ('Russia's resources are tied up on the Ukrainian battlefield'), but expects hybrid provocations to continue -- drone incursions, cyberattacks, arson, illegal migration, weather balloons -- and the line between hybrid operations and direct military action is blurring. On talks: Russia shows no serious willingness to negotiate before spring 2027; in Abu Dhabi 'the Russians will just be going through motions' and will use winter to pressure Ukraine with airstrikes. 'I don't trust them.' [CONTEXT] Polish PM Donald Tusk separately warned Russia could pursue a fresh serious escalation of its hybrid campaign in the coming months. NATO is developing plans to strike deep inside Russia if attacked (WSJ, via europesays). Estonia is fortifying its Narva border (~600 bunkers planned; defence budget +42% to EUR 2.4B, 5.4% of GDP).
sections.what_verified: 1 distinct publisher family (Axel Springer: WELT/Politico/Onet -- same group; RBC-Ukraine, UA.NEWS, mezha, ukranews, europesays, byteseu carry the same interview and hold no declared tier in the registry). PASS GATE met via primary_source_single_family: the claim IS the actor's own assessment.
sections.what_disputed: Estonia's Foreign Intelligence Service assesses Russia has NO intention of militarily attacking Estonia or another NATO member state in the coming year (Moldova1, Nov 7) -- directly undercuts the imminence read of Nauseda's warning. Nauseda himself says a conventional attack is not likely 'for now'. No Russian comment on the warning has surfaced.
sections.why_matters: A NATO president just warned Putin is about to test Article 5 -- and named the date Russia starts pretending to negotiate.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (WELT/Politico interview Nov 6, 11:00+02; Onet interview Nov 6; europesays republication Nov 7 11:59Z; ZERO 'Nauseda' mentions in any Nov 7 scan -- grep confirms) -- Lithuanian President Gitanas Nauseda: Putin 'getting closer and closer to testing Article 5'; Russia will only pretend to negotiate until spring 2027

totw_analysis: Our read: A NATO president just warned Putin is about to test Article 5 -- and named the date Russia starts pretending to negotiate. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Putin really about to test Article 5 -- or is this fear-mongering to keep NATO spending and Ukraine aid flowing?
